reviewer: Pickle: official-source winter laundry drying comparison
method: Reviewed the full draft against official sources. Korea Consumer Agency small clothes-dryer test of 8 products (2023-11-21, reproduced on Korea.kr policy briefing and the KCA Consumer Times webzine): standard-course drying time 1h43m (Hanil Electronics, shortest) to 3h06m (OA, longest), a 1h23m spread; noise 58-66 dB (avg 63 dB); per-cycle energy consumption 1,565 Wh (Hanssem) to 2,543 Wh (Hanil Electronics), a 1.6x spread; annual electricity cost at 160 cycles averages 47,000 KRW, with Minix MNMD-110G at 1,618 Wh / 41,000 KRW and Shinil SCD-T03CP at 1,590 Wh / 41,000 KRW; cotton shrinkage averaged 3.9% in total length after one standard cycle vs natural drying, so label checks and natural drying are recommended for shrink-prone items. Korea Consumer Agency dehumidifier test of 9 products (2024-07-17, Korea.kr briefing): 24-hour dehumidifying capacity 12.2-21.1 L (up to 1.7x spread), dehumidifying efficiency 2.6 L/kWh or higher for the 5 stronger products, monthly electricity cost averaging 8,000 KRW (Samsung 7,000, Boaer 10,000), Shinil's 5.7 L tank the largest. Laundry malodor bacteria: Kubota et al., Applied and Environmental Microbiology 2012 (PubMed 22367080) identified 4-methyl-3-hexenoic acid (4M3H) as the key malodor substance and Moraxella osloensis as the producing organism, with high tolerance to desiccation and UV so it survives during and after drying. Humidity and ventilation targets: KDCA national health portal winter cold-health guidance (indoor 18-20 C, ventilate 3 times daily at least 10-30 minutes, indoor humidity 40-50%) and the NIER winter indoor-air briefing on Korea.kr (comfortable humidity 40-60%, cross-ventilation at least 3 times a day for 30 minutes on an 8-hour cycle, condensation-prone homes breed mold so periodic ventilation plus dehumidifier use is advised). Electricity tariffs: Ministry of Government Legislation EasyLaw housing-electricity page (KEPCO Basic Supply Contract Appendix 1, residential low-voltage: 910 KRW basic / 120.0 KRW per kWh up to 200 kWh, 1,600 / 214.6 for 201-400 kWh, 7,300 / 307.3 above 400 kWh, plus 2.7% electric industry foundation fund and 10% VAT), giving a billed rate of about 135.56 KRW/kWh (about 136 KRW) in the first tier. All seven source URLs returned HTTP 200 on 2026-10-31 (the DOI link was replaced with the PubMed record after DOI returned 403 to automated checks). Derived figures were recorded in the research calculations: mini-dryer per-cycle cost 212 KRW (1,565 Wh) to 345 KRW (2,543 Wh) with the KCA annual average equal to 294 KRW per cycle (47,000/160) and Minix 256 KRW per cycle; a 200 W compact dehumidifier run 5 hours uses 1 kWh, about 136 KRW per day and about 4,067 KRW per month, below the KCA large-unit 8,000 KRW monthly average; one indoor drying load of 4 kg laundry at 40-50% residual moisture releases about 1.6-2.0 L (about 2 L) of water, which exceeds the roughly 0.17 kg of vapor a 24 m3 one-room at 20 C / 40% RH can hold (17.3 g/m3 saturation), so the excess condenses on cold surfaces; a 1,000 W fan heater run 3 hours costs about 407 KRW per day, equivalent to about 1.5 mini-dryer cycles. The three Coupang affiliate links were generated on 2026-10-31 and verified in-browser to resolve to the correct product pages with the AF6593875 partner tag: Minix mini dryer PRO Plus 3.5 kg (MNMD-120GR, 1,346 reviews, 526,000 KRW), Shinil 5L-10L compact dehumidifier (SDH-55LW, 179 reviews, 134,900 KRW), and Hanil AI mini clothes dryer 3 kg (HLD-G2000/HLD-2600B, 700 W, 339,000 KRW). Plan deviations: the plan's Minix 'PRO 3kg' was mapped to the verified real product PRO Plus 3.5 kg (MNMD-120GR) as the volume-1st pick; the plan's Moraxella premise (musty-cloth smell) is supported by the peer-reviewed AEM study rather than a Korean government page; the 'room humidity over 80%' framing from the plan is presented in the draft as a saturation-bound calculation rather than a cited figure.
